description: A tour of everything CreaEditor adds, and where to find it.
walkthrough.title: What's in CreaEditor
walkthrough.description: Everything CreaEditor adds, and exactly where to find it. Tip: Cmd+Shift+P opens the Command Palette, where you can type the name of any command mentioned here.
step.look.title: Creacoon look and feel
step.look.description:
Three Creacoon color themes: **Creacoon Dark**, **Creacoon Night** (almost black, easier on the eyes at night) and **Creacoon Light**. They are always at the top of the theme list.
**Where:** click the button below, or click the gear icon at the bottom left and choose **Themes > Color Theme**. Use the arrow keys to preview a theme and press Enter to keep it.
[Choose a Theme](command:workbench.action.selectTheme)
step.models.title: Your own models, no Copilot sign-in
step.models.description:
CreaEditor needs no GitHub Copilot account. Chat and agents run on your own API keys, or on models from extensions such as LiteLLM, Claude Code and Codex.
**Where:** click the button below to open the Language Models page and add a provider with your key. Then open the chat (Ctrl+Cmd+I, or the chat icon at the top of the window) and pick your model in the model picker below the input box.
[Manage Models](command:workbench.action.chat.manage)
step.gateways.title: OpenRouter and LiteLLM, auto-discovered
step.gateways.description:
Connect an OpenRouter account or your company's LiteLLM proxy:
1. Click the button below (or Cmd+Shift+P, then type **Add OpenRouter or LiteLLM Models**).
2. Press Enter to keep the OpenRouter address, or paste the address of your LiteLLM proxy instead. CreaEditor detects which one it is.
3. Type a name for the key, such as "Work key", then paste your API key.
Only the models your key is allowed to use appear in the model picker, and OpenRouter presets are added automatically.
[Add OpenRouter or LiteLLM Models](command:workbench.action.chat.addOpenRouterModel)
step.gatewayKeys.title: Several OpenRouter keys, kept apart
step.gatewayKeys.description:
Connect several OpenRouter or LiteLLM keys, each with its own spending limit. Every model shows its key, and the model picker shows what is left of each key next to its name.
A chat and all its subagents only ever use the key the chat started on.
**Good to know:** when a key reaches its limit the chat stops with the error instead of using another key.
[Add OpenRouter or LiteLLM Models](command:workbench.action.chat.addOpenRouterModel)
step.agentsWindow.title: The Agents window
step.agentsWindow.description:
A separate window made for working with AI agents. Each **session** is an agent working on one task, and several sessions can run side by side.
**How to open it:** click the button below, press Cmd+Shift+A in any CreaEditor window, or click **Try out the new Agents window** at the bottom of the Welcome page.
**What you see:** on the left the **Sessions** list, with the buttons New, Filter, Find, Toggle Agents Tree, Show AI Costs, Show Subscription Usage and Stop All Chats at the top, and the **Agents** section below it. In the middle the chat and its input box. On the right the **Changes** and **Files** of the session.
**To start:** pick your project folder in the folder button above the input box, type what you want done and press Enter.
[Open Agents Window](command:workbench.action.openAgentsWindow)
step.chatGroups.title: Director agent: several PRs at once
step.chatGroups.description:
The **Director** is a built-in agent that makes several pull requests at once. It splits the work into tasks and starts one session per task, each in its own copy of the repository (a git worktree) on its own branch, so they never get in each other's way.
1. Open the Agents window (button below, or Cmd+Shift+A).
2. Pick your repository in the folder button above the input box.
3. Click **Agent** below the input box and choose **Director**. The New Worktree checkbox disappears: the Director itself works in your folder.
4. Describe the work, for example "make PRs for issues #101, #102 and #107 on develop", press Enter and confirm the list of sessions once.
The new sessions appear in the Sessions list under one group name. The Director follows them up and ends with a table of PR links. It reads issues with the GitHub CLI, so install **gh** and sign in with **gh auth login** first.
[Open Agents Window](command:workbench.action.openAgentsWindow)
step.jira.title: Jira issues for your agents
step.jira.description:
Let agents read Jira issues directly, with their description and comments. Mention a key such as PROJ-123 in a chat, or ask for "all open bugs in sprint 12", and the agent pulls them from Jira.
**How to connect:** click the button below (or Cmd+Shift+P, **Connect Jira**) and choose **Sign In with Atlassian**. Confirm that CreaEditor may start the Atlassian server and sign in once in your browser. Agents only see what your Atlassian account can see. Works with Atlassian Cloud sites (yourcompany.atlassian.net).
**With the Director:** ask for "PRs for PROJ-12, PROJ-15 and PROJ-20 on develop" and it reads them from Jira and starts one session per issue, with the key in each branch and pull request. Jira keys also count as the issue on the AI Costs page.
[Connect Jira](command:creaeditor.connectJira)
step.agentsTree.title: Agents tree
step.agentsTree.description:
A live map of your agents. Every chat or session is a card, with lines to the subagents it started and on to their own subagents, so you see at a glance which agent started which. Each card shows the task, status, model and how long it ran, and updates live. Click a card to jump to that chat; the arrow on a card folds its subagents.
Finished, cancelled, closed and archived agents stay in the tree in a quieter grey, with their subagents folded away. Running agents are always at the top.
**Where:** in the Agents window, click **Agents** below the Sessions list (or the tree icon at the top of it) to fold the tree open or closed, and drag the line above it to resize it. Subagents show there while they run, also for sessions you have not opened. In this window, click the button below or use Cmd+Shift+P, **Show Agents Tree**.
[Show Agents Tree](command:workbench.action.chat.showAgentsTree)
step.stopAllChats.title: Stop all chats at once
step.stopAllChats.description:
**Stop All Chats** stops every running chat in every window and drops queued messages. The chats keep what they did so far.
**Where:** the stop button at the top of the Sessions list in the Agents window, or Cmd+Shift+P, **Stop All Chats**.
[Open Agents Window](command:workbench.action.openAgentsWindow)
step.costs.title: Cost per issue and per chat
step.costs.description:
The **AI Costs** page (the credit card button above the Sessions list in the Agents window) adds up what every OpenRouter and LiteLLM request cost, per issue, chat, key and repository. Its **Advanced** tab stacks filters, compares periods, and has charts, a pivot table and CSV or JSON export.
**Good to know:** every chat shows its own cost in its header; click it to see that chat on the AI Costs page.
[Show AI Costs](command:workbench.action.chat.showAiCosts)
step.budgets.title: Budgets with alerts and a hard stop
step.budgets.description:
Give a key, an issue or a repository a budget per day, week or month. A notification comes at 80% and 100%; with **Warn and Stop**, its requests are refused once the budget is used up.
[Add AI Budget](command:creaeditor.aiCosts.addBudget)
step.subscriptionAccounts.title: Several Claude and Codex accounts
step.subscriptionAccounts.description:
Pool as many Claude or Codex subscriptions as you like. When one is used up, the chat offers **Continue on ...** the next account, **Always Switch Automatically**, or **Continue When Usage Resets**.
**Good to know:** a continued chat keeps its whole conversation, and chats on different Codex accounts run side by side.
[Add Claude Account](command:workbench.action.chat.addClaudeAccount)
[Add Codex Account](command:workbench.action.chat.addCodexAccount)
step.subscriptionPicker.title: Choose the account of a chat
step.subscriptionPicker.description:
With two or more accounts, a Claude or Codex model in the model picker lists them, with what each has left. Pick one to keep the chat on it, or **Pool (Automatic)** to let it move on by itself.
[Show Subscription Usage](command:workbench.action.chat.showSubscriptionUsage)
step.subscriptionUsage.title: Usage left per subscription
step.subscriptionUsage.description:
The **Subscription Usage** page (the pulse button above the Sessions list in the Agents window) shows what is left of every Claude and Codex account and pool, and their usage over the past weeks. The status bar shows the short version, such as **Claude 62% · Codex 80%**.
**Good to know:** a warning comes at 80% and 95% of a limit; the subscription settings change it.
[Show Subscription Usage](command:workbench.action.chat.showSubscriptionUsage)
[Subscription Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22chat.subscriptionAccounts%22%5D)
step.pets.title: Creacoon pets
step.pets.description:
A pixel-art Creacoon pet that sits on the chat input in the Agents window and acts out what your agents are doing. It is off until you turn it on.
**How to turn it on:** in the Agents window, type **/creacoon-pet** in the input box and press Enter, or right-click an empty spot on the new-session screen and check **Pet**. Do the same again to turn it off.
**What it shows:** typing while the agent writes code, a magnifying glass while it researches, a clipboard while it plans, reading glasses while it reviews, a terminal while it runs tests or commands, a speech bubble while it thinks, clapping or worried when it needs your answer, and a little celebration when it is done.
Every subagent gets its own smaller pet in a different color, which leaves shortly after its work is done. Hover a small pet to see which agent it is.
**Play with it:** drag it left or right, or click it to show it some love. Your achievements are in the account menu (the person icon at the top right).
[Open Agents Window](command:workbench.action.openAgentsWindow)
step.backgrounds.title: Agents window backgrounds
step.backgrounds.description:
The Agents window has an animated background behind the chat, which stays while you work.
**How to change it:** in the Agents window, right-click an empty part of the chat area (not on a message) and choose **Set Background...**, or use Cmd+Shift+P, **Set Background**.
**Choices:** **Starry Night** (the default: twinkling Creacoon stars and now and then a shooting star), **Creacoon Pattern** (slowly drifting Creacoon marks), **Codicons**, your own **Image...**, or **No Background**. Dark and light themes each remember their own choice.
[Open Agents Window](command:workbench.action.openAgentsWindow)
step.subagents.title: Subagents that start subagents
step.subagents.description:
When an agent splits up work, its subagents can start their own subagents. They appear as cards inside the parent's card in the chat, and in the Agents tree.
A subagent that fails shows why on its card; the parent keeps going.
**Where:** click the button below to change how many levels deep they may go (setting **chat.subagents.maxNestingDepth**).
[Subagent Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22chat.subagents%22%5D)
step.metadata.title: Request metadata per key and model
step.metadata.description:
Send extra headers or body fields with your requests, for example your team or project name for the gateway's logs. Set them per API key, per model, or on a single model entry, with variables such as ${sessionId}, ${workspaceFolderName} and ${env:NAME}.
**Where:** click the button below (or Cmd+Shift+P, **Open Language Models (JSON)**) to open the file where your models are configured.
[Open Language Models (JSON)](command:workbench.action.openLanguageModelsJson)
creaeditor.config.aiCosts.budgets: Budgets for the AI costs of OpenRouter and LiteLLM requests, per key, issue or repository. Spend is counted from the costs recorded on this machine. Add and edit them on the AI Costs page or with the **Chat: Add AI Budget** command.
The requests of an OpenRouter or LiteLLM key, by its name.
The requests of chats working on an issue, e.g. `acme/web#42` or `PROJ-7`.
The requests made in a repository, e.g. `acme/web`.
creaeditor.config.aiCosts.budgets.value: The key name, issue or repository the budget is for.
creaeditor.config.aiCosts.budgets.amount: The budget in US dollars per period.
creaeditor.config.aiCosts.budgets.period: How often the budget starts over: every day, week (from Monday) or month.
creaeditor.config.aiCosts.budgets.warnAt: Percentages of the budget that show a notification, once per period.
creaeditor.config.aiCosts.budgets.hardSt: Refuse the requests of the key, issue or repository once the budget is used up.
